verses.zh: 此后，押沙龙为自己预备车马，又派五十人在他前头奔走。
verses.en: Some time later Absalom managed to acquire[NOTE:1] a chariot and horses, as well as 50 men to serve as his royal guard.[NOTE:2]

verses.zh: 押沙龙常常早晨起来，站在城门的道旁，凡有争讼要去求王判断的，押沙龙就叫他过来，问他说：「你是哪一城的人？」回答说：「仆人是以色列某支派的人。」
verses.en: Now Absalom used to get up early and stand beside the road that led to the city gate. Whenever anyone came by who had a complaint to bring to the king for arbitration, Absalom would call out to him, “What city are you from?” The person would answer, “I, your servant,[NOTE:1] am from one of the tribes of Israel.”
notes: Heb “your servant.” So also in vv. 8, 15, 21.

verses.zh: 押沙龙对他说：「你的事有情有理，无奈王没有委人听你伸诉。」
verses.en: Absalom would then say to him, “Look, your claims are legitimate and appropriate.[NOTE:1] But there is no representative of the king who will listen to you.”

verses.zh: 押沙龙又说：「恨不得我作国中的士师！凡有争讼求审判的到我这里来，我必秉公判断。」
verses.en: Absalom would then say, “If only they would make me[NOTE:1] a judge in the land! Then everyone who had a judicial complaint[NOTE:2] could come to me and I would make sure he receives a just settlement.”
notes: Heb “a complaint and a judgment.” The expression is a hendiadys.

verses.zh: 若有人近前来要拜押沙龙，押沙龙就伸手拉住他，与他亲嘴。
verses.en: When someone approached to bow before him, Absalom[NOTE:1] would extend his hand and embrace him and kiss him.
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (Absalom) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 以色列人中，凡去见王求判断的，押沙龙都是如此待他们。这样，押沙龙暗中得了以色列人的心。
verses.en: Absalom acted this way toward everyone in Israel who came to the king for justice. In this way Absalom won the loyalty[NOTE:1] of the citizens[NOTE:2] of Israel.

verses.zh: 满了四十年（有作四年的），押沙龙对王说：「求你准我往希伯仑去，还我向耶和华所许的愿。
verses.en: After four[NOTE:1] years Absalom said to the king, “Let me go and repay my vow that I made to the Lord while I was in Hebron.
notes: The MT has here “forty,” but this is presumably a scribal error for “four.” The context will not tolerate a period of forty years prior to the rebellion of Absalom. The Lucianic Greek recension (τέσσαρα ἔτη, tessara etē), the Syriac Peshitta (ʾarbaʿ sanin), and Vulgate (post quattuor autem annos) in fact have the expected reading “four years.” Most English translations follow the versions in reading “four” here, although some (e.g. KJV, ASV, NASB, NKJV), following the MT, read “forty.”

verses.zh: 因为仆人住在亚兰的基述，曾许愿说：『耶和华若使我再回耶路撒冷，我必事奉他。』」
verses.en: For I made this vow[NOTE:1] when I was living in Geshur in Aram: ‘If the Lord really does allow me to return to Jerusalem,[NOTE:2] I will serve the Lord.’”
notes: Heb “for your servant vowed a vow.” The formal court style of referring to one’s self in third person (“your servant”) has been translated here as first person for clarity.
For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

verses.zh: 王说：「你平平安安地去吧！」押沙龙就起身，往希伯仑去了。
verses.en: The king replied to him, “Go in peace.” So Absalom[NOTE:1] got up and went to Hebron.
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (Absalom) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 押沙龙打发探子走遍以色列各支派，说：「你们一听见角声就说：『押沙龙在希伯仑作王了！』」
verses.en: Then Absalom sent spies through all the tribes of Israel who said, “When you hear the sound of the horn, you may assume[NOTE:1] that Absalom rules in Hebron.”

verses.zh: 押沙龙在耶路撒冷请了二百人与他同去，都是诚诚实实去的，并不知道其中的真情。
verses.en: Now 200 men had gone with Absalom from Jerusalem. Since they were invited, they went naively and were unaware of what Absalom was planning.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “being invited and going naively and they did not know anything.”

verses.zh: 押沙龙献祭的时候，打发人去将大卫的谋士、基罗人亚希多弗从他本城请了来。于是叛逆的势派甚大；因为随从押沙龙的人民，日渐增多。
verses.en: While he was offering sacrifices, Absalom sent for Ahithophel the Gilonite, David’s adviser,[NOTE:1] to come from his city, Giloh.[NOTE:2] The conspiracy was gaining momentum, and the people were starting to side with Absalom.
notes: Traditionally, “counselor,” but this term is more often associated with psychological counseling today, so “adviser” was used in the translation instead.

Heb “Absalom sent for Ahithophel the Gilonite, the adviser of David, from his city, from Giloh, while he was sacrificing.” It is not entirely clear who (Absalom or Ahithophel) was offering the sacrifices.

verses.zh: 有人报告大卫说：「以色列人的心都归向押沙龙了！」
verses.en: Then a messenger came to David and reported, “The men of Israel are loyal to Absalom!”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “the heart of the men of Israel is with Absalom.”

verses.zh: 大卫就对耶路撒冷跟随他的臣仆说：「我们要起来逃走，不然都不能躲避押沙龙了；要速速地去，恐怕他忽然来到，加害于我们，用刀杀尽合城的人。」
verses.en: So David said to all his servants who were with him in Jerusalem,[NOTE:1] “Come on![NOTE:2] Let’s escape![NOTE:3] Otherwise no one will be delivered from Absalom! Go immediately, or else he will quickly overtake us and bring[NOTE:4] disaster on us and kill the city’s residents with the sword.”[NOTE:5]
notes: For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
Heb “and strike the city with the edge of the sword.”

verses.zh: 王的臣仆对王说：「我主我王所定的，仆人都愿遵行。」
verses.en: The king’s servants replied to the king, “We will do whatever our lord the king decides.”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “according to all that my lord the king will choose, behold your servants!”

verses.zh: 于是王带着全家的人出去了，但留下十个妃嫔看守宫殿。
verses.en: So the king and all the members of his royal court[NOTE:1] set out on foot, though the king left behind 10 concubines[NOTE:2] to attend to the palace.

verses.zh: 王出去，众民都跟随他，到伯墨哈，就住下了。
verses.en: The king and all the people set out on foot, pausing[NOTE:1] at a spot[NOTE:2] some distance away.

verses.zh: 王的臣仆都在他面前过去。基利提人、比利提人，就是从迦特跟随王来的六百人，也都在他面前过去。
verses.en: All his servants were leaving with him,[NOTE:1] along with all the Kerethites, all the Pelethites, and all the Gittites—some 600 men who had come on foot from Gath. They were leaving with[NOTE:2] the king.
notes: Heb “crossing over near the face of.”

verses.zh: 王对迦特人以太说：「你是外邦逃来的人，为甚么与我们同去呢？你可以回去与新王同住，或者回你本地去吧！
verses.en: Then the king said to Ittai the Gittite, “Why should you come with us? Go back and stay with the new[NOTE:1] king, for you are a foreigner and an exile from your own country.[NOTE:2]
notes: The word “new” is not in the Hebrew text, but is supplied in the translation to make it clear that David refers to Absalom, not himself.

verses.zh: 你来的日子不多，我今日怎好叫你与我们一同飘流、没有一定的住处呢？你不如带你的弟兄回去吧！愿耶和华用慈爱诚实待你。」
verses.en: It seems as if you arrived just yesterday. Today should I make you wander around by going with us? I go where I must go. But as for you, go back and take your men[NOTE:1] with you. May genuine loyal love[NOTE:2] protect[NOTE:3] you!”
notes: Heb “loyal love and truth.” The expression is a hendiadys.

verses.zh: 以太对王说：「我指着永生的耶和华起誓，又敢在王面前起誓：无论生死，王在哪里，仆人也必在那里。」
verses.en: But Ittai replied to the king, “As surely as the Lord lives and as my lord the king lives, wherever my lord the king is, whether it means death or life, there I[NOTE:1] will be as well!”

verses.zh: 大卫对以太说：「你前去过河吧！」于是迦特人以太带着跟随他的人和所有的妇人孩子，就都过去了。
verses.en: So David said to Ittai, “Come along then.”[NOTE:1] So Ittai the Gittite went along,[NOTE:2] accompanied by all his men and all the dependents[NOTE:3] who were with him.

verses.zh: 本地的人都放声大哭。众民尽都过去，王也过了汲沦溪；众民往旷野去了。
verses.en: All the land was weeping loudly[NOTE:1] as all these people were leaving.[NOTE:2] As the king was crossing over the Kidron Valley, all the people were leaving[NOTE:3] on the road that leads to the desert.

verses.zh: 撒督和抬　神约柜的利未人也一同来了，将　神的约柜放下。亚比亚他上来，等着众民从城里出来过去。
verses.en: Zadok and all the Levites who were with him were carrying the ark of the covenant of God. When they positioned the ark of God, Abiathar offered sacrifices until all the people had finished leaving[NOTE:1] the city.

verses.zh: 王对撒督说：「你将　神的约柜抬回城去。我若在耶和华眼前蒙恩，他必使我回来，再见约柜和他的居所。
verses.en: Then the king said to Zadok, “Take the ark of God back to the city. If I find favor in the Lord’s sight he will bring me back and enable me to see both it and his dwelling place again.

verses.zh: 倘若他说：『我不喜悦你』，看哪，我在这里，愿他凭自己的意旨待我！」
verses.en: However, if he should say, ‘I do not take pleasure in you,’ then he will deal with me in a way that he considers appropriate.”[NOTE:1]

verses.zh: 王又对祭司撒督说：「你不是先见吗？你可以安然回城；你儿子亚希玛斯和亚比亚他的儿子约拿单都可以与你同去。
verses.en: The king said to Zadok the priest, “Are you a seer?[NOTE:1] Go back to the city in peace! Your son Ahimaaz and Abiathar’s son Jonathan may go with you and Abiathar.[NOTE:2]
notes: The Greek tradition understands the Hebrew word as an imperative (“see”). Most Greek mss have ἴδετε (idete); the Lucianic recension has βλέπε (blepe). It could just as well be taken as a question: “Don’t you see what is happening?” The present translation takes the word as a question, with the implication that Zadok is a priest and not a prophet (i.e., “seer”) and therefore unable to know what the future holds.
Heb “And Ahimaaz your son, and Jonathan the son of Abiathar, two of your sons, with you.” The pronominal suffix on the last word is plural, referring to Zadok and Abiathar.

verses.zh: 我在旷野的渡口那里等你们报信给我。」
verses.en: Look, I will be waiting at the fords of the desert until word from you[NOTE:1] reaches me.”
notes: The pronoun is plural, referring to Zadok and Abiathar.

verses.zh: 于是撒督和亚比亚他将　神的约柜抬回耶路撒冷，他们就住在那里。
verses.en: So Zadok and Abiathar took the ark of God back to Jerusalem and remained there.

verses.zh: 大卫蒙头赤脚上橄榄山，一面上一面哭。跟随他的人也都蒙头哭着上去；
verses.en: As David was going up the Mount of Olives, he was weeping as he went; his head was covered and his feet were bare. All the people who were with him also had their heads covered and were weeping as they went up.

verses.zh: 有人告诉大卫说：「亚希多弗也在叛党之中，随从押沙龙。」大卫祷告说：「耶和华啊，求你使亚希多弗的计谋变为愚拙！」
verses.en: Now David[NOTE:1] had been told, “Ahithophel has sided with the conspirators who are with Absalom.” So David prayed,[NOTE:2] “Make the advice of Ahithophel foolish, O Lord.”
notes: The translation follows 4QSama, part of the Greek tradition, the Syriac Peshitta, Targum, and Vulgate in reading “and to David,” rather than MT וְדָוִד (vedavid, “and David”). As Driver points out, the Hebrew verb הִגִּיד (higgid, “he related”) never uses the accusative for the person to whom something is told (S. R. Driver, Notes on the Hebrew Text and the Topography of the Books of Samuel, 316).

verses.zh: 大卫到了山顶、敬拜　神的地方，见亚基人户筛，衣服撕裂，头蒙灰尘来迎接他。
verses.en: When David reached the summit, where he used to worship God, Hushai the Arkite met him with his clothes torn and dirt on his head.

verses.zh: 大卫对他说：「你若与我同去，必累赘我；
verses.en: David said to him, “If you leave[NOTE:1] with me you will be a burden to me.

verses.zh: 你若回城去，对押沙龙说：『王啊，我愿作你的仆人；我向来作你父亲的仆人，现在我也照样作你的仆人。』这样，你就可以为我破坏亚希多弗的计谋。
verses.en: But you will be able to counter the advice of Ahithophel if you go back to the city and say to Absalom, ‘I will be your servant, O king! Previously I was your father’s servant, and now I will be your servant.’

verses.zh: 祭司撒督和亚比亚他岂不都在那里吗？你在王宫里听见甚么，就要告诉祭司撒督和亚比亚他。
verses.en: Zadok and Abiathar the priests will be there with you.[NOTE:1] Everything you hear in the king’s palace[NOTE:2] you must tell Zadok and Abiathar the priests.
notes: Heb “Will not Zadok and Abiathar the priests be there with you?” The rhetorical question draws attention to the fact that Hushai will not be alone.
Heb “from the house of the king.”

verses.zh: 撒督的儿子亚希玛斯，亚比亚他的儿子约拿单，也都在那里。凡你们所听见的可以托这二人来报告我。」
verses.en: Furthermore, their two sons are there with them, Zadok’s son Ahimaaz and Abiathar’s son Jonathan. You must send them to me with any information you hear.”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and you must send by their hand to me every word which you hear.” Both of the second person verb forms are plural with Zadok, Abiathar, and Hushai being the understood subjects.

verses.zh: 于是，大卫的朋友户筛进了城；押沙龙也进了耶路撒冷。
verses.en: So David’s friend Hushai arrived in the city, just as Absalom was entering Jerusalem.
